# Pass 4 — Batch D: SECURITY-001 and Annex K Authority Decision

## Decision

The former derivation from SECURITY-001 to Annex K is withdrawn. It created a circular authority claim because Annex K simultaneously stated that it translated SECURITY-001 and could not redefine SECURITY invariants.

The repaired authority chain is:

| Function | Owner | Authority class | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constitutional hierarchy and execution constraints | AEON-001 and applicable constitutional schedules | Constitutional source | Security cannot displace constitutional constraints. |
| Security doctrine, invariants, threat interpretation, integrity, trust and adversarial classifications | SECURITY-001 | Domain source | Does not execute, self-authorise intervention, or override ETHICS. |
| Runtime-facing security-boundary interface | Annex K | Bounded constitutional source | Consumes SECURITY doctrine and emits boundary inputs; does not define SECURITY doctrine or procedure. |
| Incident intake, evidence custody, routing, containment procedure, logging and closure | OPERATIONS | Derived operational authority | Must preserve domain-signal provenance and cannot create substantive authority. |
| Contested authority, scope and cross-domain conflict | ARBITRATION | Domain source | Selects among admissible pathways; does not create an otherwise absent mandate. |

Effective delegated authority is the intersection of the originating mandate, the delegate's role limits, and every applicable governance constraint. Agreement, capability, credential possession, evaluator status, technical success, or access is evidence only; none creates authority.

## Placement review

| Required element | Finding |
|---|---|
| Failure mechanism | A security-domain charter and a constitutional interface each claimed to derive from the other, enabling circular authority and obscuring which layer owned procedure. |
| Governance layer | Domain doctrine and constitutional runtime interface, with consequential operational and arbitral routing. |
| Instruments inspected | AEON-001, Annex K, SECURITY-001, OPERATIONS-001, OPERATIONS-003, OPERATIONS-008, and ARBITRATION-001. |
| Existing adjacent controls | SECURITY-001 §3.5.1; Annex K §§1.1–1.3 and 2.4.3–2.4.4; OPERATIONS-003 incident lifecycle; OPERATIONS-008 adversarial-evaluation procedure; ARBITRATION-001 legitimacy and scope validation. |
| Repair made | SECURITY-001 now states its constitutional parent and Annex K interface without deriving from Annex K. Annex K expressly limits its source authority to the constitutional interface. Metadata and provenance footers were normalised. |
| Remaining consolidation | Annex K still contains operationally detailed material, principally in §§2.2–2.5 and §§3.1–3.7. The next consolidation batch must relocate or reduce it by reference to OPERATIONS-008, OPERATIONS-003, and applicable operational supplements, without copying procedure into SECURITY-001. |

## Non-derogable routing rules retained

- SECURITY cannot override ETHICS non-derogables.
- SECURITY cannot override constitutional execution constraints or the LATTICE constitutional boundary.
- OPERATIONS may route, preserve evidence and run procedure; it cannot convert those functions into substantive authority.
- Ambiguity about authority, scope, or incompatible applicable obligations routes to ARBITRATION.
- Annex K emits boundary conditions and integrity signals only; it does not release a hold, approve action, or create a containment exception.
